**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** I reviewed this as a draft, as dispatched, and left the draft state as you set it.

## What looks good

- **The air rule cannot cut the part.** The "in air" test is not the part guard. Every in-plane link, straight or edge route, must also stay inside the certified cutter-centre area: `chord_clears(center, ..)` in `level_order::linkable` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_order.rs:268`) and `chord_ok(cen, ..)` in `ring_links::link` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs:129`). That area is the machining region eroded by tool radius + stock-to-leave (`non_sliver_center` = `region.offset(-off)`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_plan.rs:41`; `off = tool_diameter/2 + stock_to_leave`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:259`). Its inner boundary is the part wall, so a centre on any accepted chord stays at least one tool radius from the part and the disc cannot gouge it. The 0.1-radius threshold (`ring_links.rs:24`) only decides where there is genuinely no material, to skip the uncut-stock test.
- **The edge route stays inside the area and touches, never crosses.** `edge_route` walks the loops of the same `center` and proves every chord with the same `linkable` (`level_order.rs:128-135`), so each chord clears the cutter-centre area. `through` inserts each walk vertex that lies on a chord (`ring_links.rs:255-284`), and `chord_crosses_path` reads a shared vertex as a touch (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/waterscan.rs:19`), so a piece that ends on the edge is touched at a shared vertex. The route has no loop that can fail to terminate: bounded `for` loops over loops, attach points (`ATTACHES = 6`) and vertices, no `while`. `ring_links.rs` has no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic`, `unsafe`, `std::process`, `std::fs`, `std::env` or `std::net`.
- **Every in-plane lift is named.** For a ring area `pass_link` always calls `ring_links::link` and, on `Err`, tallies the reason before lifting to `hop_z` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs:164-183`). The reasons are the stay-down limit, the part, a fixture, a crossing and uncut stock (`ring_links.rs:32-50`). The new pins assert `named == lifts` on the synthetic and fig8 cases. No note says "Auto": `ring_side::resolve` replaces Auto with Inside/Outside before the notes are built.
- **The pocket path is byte-for-byte.** When `ring_links` is `None`, the `pass_link` refactor is equivalent to the old `Clearance`/`Retract`/`KeepDown` arms; I checked each arm. `pocket_over_with_relief` sets `ring_links` only when `side.start != Auto` and `for_side` returns `Some` only when `around_part` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs:88`), and the 2D Offset op is the keep/around-part path (`OpType::Offset2D`, strategy `Waterline`, `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:1043-1081`). A 2D Pocket with Inside/On containment keeps `around_part: false` and so is byte-for-byte (see the note below for Outside containment).
- **Pins are real gouge checks:** the motion pins run the shape mask `assert_no_overcut` and `verify::crossed_pairs`; the fig8 heavy pins check no crossing warning and no full-width move.
- Decision doc matches `docs/decisions/README.md`; new source module has a provenance line; `ring_links.rs` is 322 lines.

## Results (merged with main)

Trial merge of `968fa46d7` with `origin/main` `b2ff0ef1b`: clean (the PR was dispatched against `cd0222d9c`; main advanced by one unrelated merge, #3059 chamfer, on files this PR does not touch). Built locally on the review box, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`, sccache; no self-hosted runner was used.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pass_start_levels`: 13 passed, 0 failed (includes `ring_links::start_side_rings_do_not_lift`, `ring_links::dogbone_start_side_lifts`, `ring_links::lift_reason_is_named`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start`: 6 passed, 0 failed, 5 heavy ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (`light build (release --no-run)` 2s; `motion light: lib` 327s; `motion light: adaptive_troch_island` 34s; `motion light: adaptive_troch_neck` 13s; `motion light: adaptive_troch_parallel` 9s; `app light: pocket_pass_start` 11s). These light twins are adaptive/pocket checks; none covers the changed offset ring law.
- Targeted heavy step (P1 safety floor), `app heavy: offset_pass_start` (release, `--ignored`): 5 passed, 0 failed in 59 s (`fig8_outside_offset_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge`, `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`, `fig8_inside_offset_names_each_full_width_cut`, `fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing`, and the new `lifts::fig8_start_sides_lift_only_with_a_named_reason`). I ran the binary with the gate's own release `--ignored` command; the `cargo xtask gate heavy --only` driver stalled in plan computation, so I did not use the wrapper.
- Example catalogs: not re-run, because no catalog case touches the changed law. No catalog case is a round-a-part `Offset2D`; the only offset-rings case (`examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket`) is a 2D Pocket with Inside/On containment, which keeps `ring_links: None` and so is byte-for-byte. Step 5's example-catalog requirement is therefore not applicable.

## Requested before merge

- None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The ring/join law is selected for any `around_part` area with a chosen pass start (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:351-354`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs:88`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_order.rs:106`), and `around_part` is true for any Clearing op with Outside containment and a stock. That includes a 2D Pocket with Outside containment, as exercised by `crates/app/tests/pocket_pass_start.rs` (`pocket_op` sets `Containment::Outside`). Such a pocket's joins and pass links now take the ring law, while the PR body says "2D Pocket Inside and Outside do not change (#3752)". It is safe (every link is proved, else a named lift), but it is not pinned here. Please confirm the intended scope, and add a pin or narrow the gate to the Offset2D op.
- `max_stay_down` is checked on the pass-to-pass link (`ring_links.rs:118`) but not on the planner join (`level_order::linkable`/`edge_route`), so the new edge route can make one continuous in-plane pass longer than the user's stay-down limit. This matches the pre-existing straight join, but the edge route can be much longer; confirm it is intended.
- For a ring area the ring law overrides `Link::Clearance`/`KeepDown`; a failed link lifts to `hop_z` (retract), not `clearance_z`. The decision doc records this; confirm it suits users who chose Clearance.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Needs changes before merge.** The link law is sound and the pins are good. One finding: the ring law also changes 2D Adaptive output, which #3747 does not cover and no pin guards.

Review at the safety-floor level (2D toolpath motion). Trial merge with `origin/main` at `cd0222d9c`: clean, no conflicts. Built and tested locally.

### What looks good
- `ring_links::link` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs:107-150`) proves each in-plane link in a fixed order: stay-down limit, certified area, no crossing, then each sample in air or over a cleared column. It reads the stock state from the emitted moves at that depth (`plunge_law::column_cleared`, moves at or below `z` only). It does not read only the geometry.
- The "cut floor" reach is 0.9 tool radii in the ladder (`r * SWATH / (1 - CORE)`, then `column_cleared` takes `(1 - CORE)` of it) and in the planner (`reach = SWATH * tool_r`). The two laws agree. A link sample can cut at most 0.9 radii into uncut stock. It never cuts at full width.
- The air law is conservative. Air starts 0.1 radii outside the stock footprint, and no footprint gives no air (`RingLinks::new`).
- Each failed link lifts with a named reason through `st.tally.lift`. `LinkTally::say` runs for each pass link value, so a `Retract` op shows the `link:` notes too.
- The pins count the lifts from the moves and compare the count with the named count. Thus one unnamed lift fails the pin. The pins also assert no overcut (shape mask) and no crossing feeds. The clamp pin asserts `avoid_hits` is empty.
- Old project files: there is no `Links::RINGS` seed and no change in `crates/app/src`. Old and new files get the same path.
- A pocket keeps its links: `Pocket` builds `StartSide` with `around_part: false`, and `ring_links::for_side` returns `None` for it.
- No logic overlap with #3746 (entry): this PR does not touch `approach.rs` or `descent*.rs`.

### Results (merged with main, locally, CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6, -j 6)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion --test pass_start_levels` (includes the 3 new pins) | 13 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-motion --test pass_start_engagement` | 6 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-motion --lib machining2d` | 277 passed, 0 failed, 22 ignored |
| `camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start` (debug) | 6 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Pin readings (`ring_links`, one level): disc Inside / Outside / Auto 0 lifts and 0 re-entries; dog bone Inside / Outside 0 / 0; clamp Inside 3 lifts and Outside 26 lifts, all named "fixture".

### Heavy lanes
- `app heavy: offset_pass_start` (release, `--ignored`): ok, 5 passed, 0 failed, run by this review (696 s).
- The heavy dry run maps the diff to more lanes, because `motion` reaches the `app` heavy lanes. By the coordinator's order, only the targeted step ran. The other reached lanes were not run by this review, and the cut gate checks them.

fig8 lift reasons (this review, release run of the new pin):
```
fig8 Inside: 6 lift(s) inside a level, 6 named
link: 3 time(s) the in-plane link would cross a cut planned on that plane (first lift at (-51.500, 58.674), Z 12.000)
link: 3 time(s) the in-plane link would leave the area that keeps the tool off the part (first lift at (-46.500, 123.542), Z 12.000)
fig8 Outside: 12 lift(s) inside a level, 12 named
link: 6 time(s) the in-plane link would cross a cut planned on that plane (first lift at (47.429, -39.000), Z 12.000)
link: 6 time(s) the in-plane link would leave the area that keeps the tool off the part (first lift at (46.488, 123.257), Z 12.000)
```

### Requested before merge
1. **Scope: the ring law reaches 2D Adaptive.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:351-354` sets `ring_links` for each strategy when the resolved side is Inside or Outside and `around_part` is true. `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:997` sets `around_part: around_band` for `Adaptive2D` too, with `strategy: PocketStrategy::Adaptive`. Thus a 2D Adaptive (Spiral) with "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside round a part now links its passes by the ring law, not by its stored pass link. The links are proved, so this is not a gouge. But it changes posted G-code of an op that #3747 does not cover, with no pin and no changelog row. The PR body says the change is for 2D Offset only. The `pocket_avoid.rs:254-259` site has the same question for the avoid path.
   - Class: a law keyed on `around_part` reaches each op that sets `around_part`.
   - One rule that closes the class: enable the ring law only for the ring strategies, with one predicate (for example the strategy test of `ring_side::resolves`: `Waterline | OffsetRings`) that `pocket.rs` and `pocket_avoid.rs` both use. If 2D Adaptive must take the law, then add a pin for it, a changelog row and a line in the decision file.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **The fig8 lifts are partly a planner gap.** All 18 lifts are named, so this is not a blocker. But no lift names a fixture, and fig8 has none. Nine lifts are "would cross a cut" and nine are "would leave the area". `ladder_links::pass_link` tries only the straight chord (`ring_links::link`). It does not try the `edge_route` that the planner uses, or a route over the cut floor. By the maintainer's #3741 rule, a lift is permitted only when *each* in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Please file a `P1` follow-up issue (by #3741) for an edge or floor route at the ladder pass link. Name it in the PR body.
- The note text says "instead of the keep-down level/pass link" (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:170`). An op with the stored `Retract` link now shows it too. The user did not ask for keep-down. Consider a neutral word ("in-plane").
- When the straight chord leaves the certified area, the fixture test reads only the samples (`ring_links.rs:128-133`). A chord that touches a keep-out between two samples is named "part", not "fixture". The lift still happens, so only the name can be wrong.
- In the planner, the join legs go into the pass walk. `fillet_corners` (blend turns) and `fit_arcs` later change those corners. The `Legal` region keeps them off the part. The air and cut-floor proof is not run again on the rounded corner. The risk is small (a fillet stays between the two proved legs), but no pin covers blend turns with a join leg.
- The dog bone Outside pin shows `entry: a second dive at the pass start (39.929, -29.000)`. This is entry work for #3746.
- #3746 sequencing: the #3746 work in progress adds a `known-fail #3747` marker (`fig8_outside_offset_has_no_plunge_into_material`). When this PR merges, #3747 closes, and the gate fails a known-fail marker whose issue is closed. The worker of #3746 must change that marker. The two PRs also add fields next to each other in `levels.rs`, `pocket_emit.rs`, `pocket.rs` and `pocket_avoid_level.rs`, so expect text conflicts but no logic overlap.
- `levels.rs` is over 400 lines (457 -> 460). Noted only.
- Process: the body has `Changelog:`, ends `Fixes #3747`, and has no process file. Commit subjects are conventional.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
